spec.title: ZAP: canonical data, events, and future viewing

status.comment: Normative canonical-data and machine-view requirements for the Owner-authorized Rust MVP. Existing prototype capabilities remain historical evidence; the future interactive canvas remains separate work.

boundary.title: 1. Data contract and truthful implemented surface

p.DATA-STATUS: This document defines required ZAP data properties and the path to external tools. The legacy container format is schema zap/1 and preserves the complete imported MUP plan, task contracts, and separate ZAP extensions. The current Rust store and its explicit epochs follow ZAP-RUST-STORAGE.xml; legacy bytes retain their own interpretation. A field in a draft schema does not imply an implemented transition. Every available operation has an explicit contract, handler, and validation; other requirements remain planned.

p.SUPPORTED-SUBSET: The implemented operation set is published from actual handler, schema, and route registries through capabilities and the command contract. Unknown commands, versions, fields, and rule operators are refused. The CLI and backend do not infer authority from actor labels; dry run and observation are not described as performed or accepted product actions.

p.PROTOTYPE-OPERATIONS: The historical prototype's five original commands and later migration, charter, capture, snapshot, repair, promotion, automatic coordination, and authenticated backend behavior remain migration and characterization inputs. Rust capabilities count as implemented only when their own registries and evidence publish them. Import and installation do not start NEXT. The interactive canvas, IDE plugin, and a custom IDE are outside this package.

p.RUST-MVP-DATA-SURFACE: The Rust MVP must represent StrategicPlan and Lowering revisions, obligations and stage debt, forks, capabilities and desired or resolved profiles, packet and attempt lineage, claims, DispatchIntents and ExternalJobHandles, liveness and checkpoints, WeakBundles and encounter journals, DreamBranches, economics, holds, stop state, completion blockers, and their provenance. Planned schema text is not implementation evidence.

p.STORAGE-OWNERSHIP: Personal execution progress belongs to a ZAP context bound to the user and exact checkout. Shared requirements, accepted project facts, code, evidence, and intentionally shared campaign inputs remain in the repository. No shared queue of personal sessions is created. The pilot imports a separate copy of the seed and task contracts; it does not rewrite MUP plan.toml, settings, GOAL, statuses, or active constraints.

p.IMMUTABLE-BASE: The initial base preserves source files with hashes of exact bytes, source names, and captured identities. The parsed model is bound to that base. New changes are append-only events; the base is not rewritten under a new interpretation. Projections and acceleration snapshots derive from a specific base and accepted event sequence.

p.PROTOTYPE-FILES: In the legacy prototype format, base.json with schema zap/1 contains the complete MUP plan, task contracts, and raw captures with base64 source bytes and SHA-256. events.jsonl begins with store.imported, binding the journal to the base hash. Later rows carry seq, revision, previous_revision, event_id, kind, reason, payload, and command_sha256. Commands use base_revision; the ZAP projection revision is separate from the imported plan revision. These are legacy local-store names; the Rust store and implemented HTTP interface have separate public contracts.

p.LOSSLESS-IMPORT: Import preserves every mandate, node, identity, order, hierarchy, dependency, state, acceptance criterion, evidence item, task, and unknown source-format extension. Values are not guessed from titles or simplified during conversion. Type and representation changes have explicit source mappings; retained source bytes allow later verification of material not yet interpreted.

p.PILOT-DENOMINATOR: The known NEXT pilot expects 425 nodes and 212 task contracts at the captured source state. Individual identities, values, links, and contract contents are verified; matching two counts is insufficient. New work_type, maturity, and knowledge annotations are separate and may remain unspecified. Prior acceptance is preserved as a sourced imported assertion, not a new ZAP verification.

p.IMPORT-AUTHORITY: Imported Owner commands and decisions retain provenance and require explicit charter-preparation classification. Deserialization neither loses them nor makes them executable. The NEXT start prohibition, D-022, and external-action constraints remain visible. Import cannot create activation evidence; a source file owner field is not a trusted control channel.

p.GRAPH-IDENTITY: Intent, expected-outcome revisions, value and feasibility assessments, mandates, obligations, work, facts, decisions, unknown regions, approaches, and evidence have stable identities. Renaming does not change identity, and identity is not reused for another subject. Node kind, state, work purpose, delivery route, declared maturity, achieved stage, current value, and knowledge applicability are independent. A declared classification proves no stage, and child count proves no parent acceptance.

p.GRAPH-RELATIONS: Relations show which requirement work serves, which sources support a conclusion, which evidence supports a claim, which premises a decision uses, and what it changes. Contradiction, replacement, and invalidation preserve prior records. A relation needs defined endpoints and clear meaning; similar wording does not create a dependency.

p.NORMATIVE-AND-MEASURED: Normative fact text and specification status remain separate from current-state observations and accepted evidence. An observation names the measured subject, method, and applicability. A conclusion references its premises. Acceptance lists proven obligations and required check results. A link, confident prose, or third-party PASS does not raise status.

p.SOURCE-HANDLES: A source reference contains a stable handle, location or spec anchor, source kind, and captured content identity. Verification also binds inputs, dependencies, fixtures, command, toolchain, target, and environment. A URL or commit without that scope is not reproducibility. An unavailable source remains unresolved rather than verified.

p.KNOWLEDGE-AND-SCOPE: unexamined, bounded, evidenced, and invalidated apply to a specific unknown region and question. An authorized scope exclusion is stored separately. A closed graph does not prove absolute knowledge completeness. Missing links and assessments remain unknown; an empty set is not proof of no risk.

p.DEPENDENT-INVALIDATION: Changed captured source content marks dependent evidence and conclusions for reassessment without erasing acceptance history or invalidating unrelated results. The graph identifies known impact; the coordinator assesses whether recorded dependencies are semantically complete. Incomplete input closure requires affected verification, not an automatic full product run.

p.LOWERING-DATA: A lowering result binds to an expected-outcome revision and maps its obligations to child work, evidence, and integration acceptance. Each deferral has a concrete scope and obligation. Outcome revision records each prior obligation disposition, successor, remaining difference, and authority. Readiness uses required intermediate guarantees: an accepted experiment is not a finished interface. Missing coverage remains a defect even when every created task is done.

p.EXECUTION-LINEAGE-DATA: Lowering, packet, logical operation, attempt, message, artifact, evidence, verification, and acceptance have separate stable identities and causal relations. A packet digest protects bytes but does not replace packet_id, parent Lowering revision, semantic-contract identity, render profile, or derived_from and supersedes lineage. A rerender or retry does not erase earlier candidates or receipts.

p.DETACHED-BRANCH-DATA: A strategic fork, DreamBranch, execution workspace, and source-control branch are different subjects. Dream data binds a live base revision and stores only its proposed delta, assumptions, questions, estimates, and calculated effects. It remains detached from live scope, work, approval consumption, and holds until an exact authorized application event.

p.ADAPTIVE-REVIEW-INPUTS: A review has review_id, a link to the prior material review, input signals, and captures of base hash, ZAP revision or cursor, intent, charter, prior outcome, route, material sources, and affected jobs. Transition acceptance checks every material input for currency. Journal CAS alone does not prove an external service unchanged or a worker stopped. An ordinary session change does not require a review.

p.ADAPTIVE-REVIEW-ASSESSMENT: The record contains unknown-region changes before and after, newly found questions, source dependencies, affected conclusion closure, and an assessment of closure completeness. It preserves comparable alternatives and grounded or unknown assessments of Owner value, feasibility under named conditions, remaining cost, and risk. Historical truth, current applicability, and present value are distinct. An incomplete map is not presented as exhaustive analysis.

p.ADAPTIVE-REVIEW-TRANSITION: A decision binds the selected alternative, concise rationale, actual authority, before and after outcome revisions, tradeoffs, and preserved benefit. The transition lists affected-obligation dispositions, task, contract, dependency, priority, acceptance, and deferral changes, preserved evidence, and a live-job plan. Stop-rule assessment, expected revision, and command identity are separate. Proposal, accepted transition, and confirmed job effect are distinct states. A meaningful keep-route decision records its basis without artificial plan change.

p.ADAPTIVE-VIEW: The viewer shows original intent, prior and current expected outcomes, preserved benefit, tradeoffs, unmet properties, and reasons priorities changed. Fog expansion, stale premises, the next experiment, and reversibility remain visible. Results distinguish original success, authorized revised success, partial benefit, and unattainability under known conditions. Stored decisions and transitions supply this view; the viewer does not invent it with a new model call.

p.ADAPTIVE-WIRE-STATUS: The adaptive cycle has separate intent, outcome, and review proposals and policy-admitted application events. It preserves stale captures, essential obligations, evidence applicability, and live-job reconciliation. The command contract and capabilities list only actual event types; a proposal is not application.

p.COMMAND-PRECONDITIONS: A data-changing command names the logical object, expected base or projection revision, request identity, and causal references. The receiver validates operation support, inputs, preconditions, and separate required authority. A stale revision yields an explicit conflict for rereading instead of overwriting unknown changes. Data idempotency does not make repetition of an external effect safe.

p.IDEMPOTENT-COMMAND: One idempotency key identifies one logical command and its content. An exact retry returns the known result without another transition; different content under the key is refused. The key is not replaced to repeat an operation with unknown outcome. Recovery uses receipts, external-operation identity, and actual postconditions when supported.

p.APPEND-LOG: Accepted changes form an ordered append-only sequence with event identities, revisions, and causal references. An operation records its whole defined transition or leaves a detectable incomplete tail. The format distinguishes complete events from a partial last row; the parser does not ignore middle corruption or treat a partial tail as a completed command.

p.PROTOTYPE-EVENTS: The kernel composes explicit core, control, domain, knowledge, and runtime handler registries. Every extension event belongs to exactly one data, action, or trusted-observation route; internal control events are unavailable to public callers. Replay uses the same registry and reproduces admitted history without reauthentication or external effects.

p.LOG-RECOVERY: Recovery finds the last complete confirmed boundary, preserves corruption evidence, and reconciles the related command result. Damaged bytes are not silently deleted to make replay pass. Explicit storage mechanisms define repair and authority. While outcome is ambiguous, no external effect repeats. A plain file does not promise exclusion of arbitrary concurrent writers.

p.DETERMINISTIC-REPLAY: One reducer version, immutable base, and confirmed event sequence produce one projection. Replay calls no LLM, network, current clock, executor, or external command. Time, semantic assessments, and observations enter as sourced stored data. Changed computation rules require an explicit version and verified migration; old events are not silently reinterpreted.

p.SNAPSHOT-PROVENANCE: A snapshot records base identity, reducer version, event boundary, and verifiable projection identity. It accelerates reading and can be rebuilt from canonical data. It neither creates authority nor replaces a missing journal. Identity mismatch requires fetching the correct data rather than joining incompatible fragments.

p.SEMANTIC-EVENTS: A decision or semantic-condition assessment stores concise rationale, sources, and scope. Replay reproduces its existence and effects without claiming to re-prove language truth. Reassessment on new data creates a new record and may supersede the old conclusion while preserving history. Private reasoning chains are not required journal data.

authority.title: 5. Separation of Owner control and editable data

p.TRUSTED-CONTROL-BOUNDARY: The control service authenticates an opaque credential or configured host principal outside the campaign store and binds role, campaign, and allowed commands. Reader is separate from owner and coordinator; the agent route remains data-only. Secrets do not enter the journal, JSON command, packet, argv, or environment. This boundary does not claim protection from an OS administrator or same-user process already able to read protected configuration.

p.OWNER-COMMAND-PROJECTION: The journal may store a verified reference to an accepted Owner command and its effects. Provenance is checked through the control boundary; editing its textual projection does not create new authority. Schema validation alone is insufficient. A successful rule assessment does not prove stop delivery to every executor.

p.STOP-OBSERVABILITY: Condition assessment, the whole-campaign stop decision, prevention of new launches, and actual safe state of running jobs are observed separately. Unfinished jobs remain visible during a stop. Result collection and preparation for an Owner decision are visible authorized completion work; a third architectural attempt cannot be hidden inside those records.

p.RULE-UNKNOWN: needs_evidence is the explicit result of missing assessment inputs. Expression evaluation preserves unknown according to declared operator logic and refuses unsupported operators. The executor investigates required data without launching the conditionally blocked action. Unknown is not serialized as false, an empty string, or an absent rule.

p.PROTOTYPE-STOP-FIXTURES: evaluate-stop accepts only an unapproved zap-stop/1 example with status example_unapproved. A rule has id, when, run scope, and timing before_action or before_next_action; semantic values are true, false, or null. failed_approaches with gte 2 finds two confirmed failures for any one problem in campaign history. The result analyzes an example and neither activates runtime policy nor authorizes an action. A late check reports too_late.

p.FUTURE-RESUME-CONTROL: Resume binds the exact active pause ID and hash, separately verified delivery and actual-safe-state acknowledgements, and an Owner credential. A one-shot exception binds one action identity, payload, and source set. Only the Owner changes an approach epoch; history remains.

p.LOGICAL-AND-PHYSICAL-STATE: Campaign state describes obligations and controlled work progress; a session is current coordinator context; a run or job is a concrete execution with observed results. Their identities and completion reasons are separate. Closing a window or lacking narration does not finish a job; job completion does not accept an obligation; resource wait is neither policy pause nor campaign completion.

p.RESOURCE-WAIT: A resource record names the unavailable capability, observation, affected operations, and known retry condition. Unknown recovery time remains explicit. Background waiting and wakeup are shown only when an authorized runtime is actually configured. Session changes preserve attempts, approaches, and evidence; secrets and full sensitive provider responses stay out of the journal.

p.PROJECT-LOCAL-SPLIT: After acceptance, durable project knowledge receives a permanent repository source; the local record retains its acceptance provenance. Personal settings, unfinished reasoning, machine facts, and local campaign progress are not published automatically. Data from another worker or documentation repository is read through a captured source and agreed ownership rather than a shared status string.

p.CANVAS-EXPERIENCE: Owner clarification of 2026-09-13: the future viewer is a full interactive canvas for a large graph with convenient navigation. Selected-node content is read in place without losing graph position. Three.js is a proposed rendering candidate; engine and dimensionality are selected during viewer implementation from capability and measurement. The Rust MVP data contract must support this future client; the application remains separate work.

p.LARGE-GRAPH-NAVIGATION: The canvas supports pan and zoom, search with result focus, hierarchy and dependency navigation, collapse and expansion, filters, navigation history, and saved viewpoints. Overview and detail use the same stable IDs. New events and renames do not reset selection or position. Camera, panels, and bookmarks are view state, not mandate or acceptance changes.

p.IN-CANVAS-NODE-DETAIL: The selected-node inspector shows available full content: work goal and steps, criteria and checks, sources, related specifications, facts, decisions and reasons, evidence, dependencies, maturity, deferrals, and change history. A summary does not replace the detailed contract; unavailable content is explicit. Following a related node preserves context. Text loads through verified source handles, not an arbitrary path from untrusted task prose.

p.CLICKABLE-ENTITY-DETAIL: Every material canvas entity—a node, edge, known or unknown region, job, or decision—opens assembled detail in place. The response includes available content, provenance, and history, and distinguishes missing, unloaded, unavailable, and stale data. The backend does not invent explanations for data gaps and preserves selected-entity identity.

p.CANVAS-DATA-ACCESS: The backend provides separate overview or subgraph, search, node-detail, dependency, revision-comparison, readiness, why, packet, and resume queries with stable identities, revision, scope, completeness, and cursor. Large graphs load incrementally while keeping every result reachable. Unloaded, filtered, unavailable, excluded, and semantically unknown regions are distinct. Clustering and levels of detail do not rewrite the canonical plan or require a model call for navigation.

p.STRATEGY-MAP-METAPHOR: The Owner proposed Heroes 3 and StarCraft as the interface metaphor: explored map, research frontier, and fog beyond it. Known areas are clear and saturated; transparency, saturation, boundaries, and optional fog show transition to the unknown. Unknown detail is not painted as existing nodes. A colorful center suggests explored territory but camera proximity does not prove knowledge; known areas may still contain gaps or stale data. ZAP creates its own graphics and symbols; game names are experience references, not assets to copy.

p.HEROES-ART-DIRECTION: Additional Owner clarification of 2026-09-13: the visual style is game-like with an explicit Heroes 3 reference. It envisions a vivid illustrated map, recognizable objects and icons, styled paths, fog, and game-like detail panels. Beauty, clarity of important signals, and readability are joint criteria. Decorative layers preserve graph and text legibility across scales; a usable inspector shows the full node contract. This future canvas art direction remains separate from the current backend.

p.ORTHOGONAL-VISUAL-CHANNELS: Color, saturation, geometry, outline, icons, edge styling, and text jointly distinguish independent properties. A possible initial mapping uses clarity or fog for knowledge, shape for work purpose, outline and icon for execution state, and edge style for relation meaning. A legend explains the mapping; critical information does not depend on color alone. Labels and inspector remain readable with effects enabled, and motion or decorative fog can be reduced.

p.KNOWLEDGE-VISUAL-DISTINCTIONS: Both visual and machine data distinguish an unexamined region, bounded research question, evidenced knowledge, information that lost applicability, deliberate scope exclusion, and client data not yet loaded. Fog returning after a fact or goal change is an observed knowledge change, not a loading error. Filtering and collapsing hide a view without changing knowledge or acceptance status.

p.VIEWER-SCOPE: The future viewer may use Qwik 2, but its data contract remains framework-independent. The Rust MVP must implement the machine-data and event backend; the canvas app, IDE plugin, and custom IDE remain separate work. Machine inputs and outputs expose strategy, work, facts, decisions, unknown regions, evidence, approaches, stages, debt, packets, runtime, economics, and stop reasons without treating prose as protocol. Semantic properties are separate from rendering colors, geometry, and camera position.

p.SNAPSHOT-AND-CURSOR: A client receives a snapshot with campaign, base, schema, revision, and last-included-event cursor identity. Continuation references that cursor and sequence. A cursor is journal position, not wall-clock time. Duplicate events are recognized by identity; foreign base, gap, or unknown cursor requires an explicit gap response and an appropriate snapshot.

p.STREAM-RECOVERY: The authenticated backend serves snapshot and resumable event tail or SSE under one base, revision, and cursor identity. Page cursors bind query and revision. Gaps, foreign bases, and stale pages are explicit. A pending final fragment is visible to a reader as the committed-state diagnostic boundary but blocks mutations; middle corruption is not masked.

p.PLANNED-EVENT-FAMILIES: The external surface includes plan-change, decision, invalidation, rule-assessment, campaign-pause, resource-wait, worker-result, acceptance, and fact-promotion events. Implemented registries and capabilities are authoritative for actual families, wire identifiers, and versions. An unknown type is never presented as a successfully applied transition.

p.VIEWER-EXPLANATIONS: The viewer shows stored rationale and source references. Opening an item does not trigger new semantic assessment or rewrite an event. A composite conclusion exposes premises, applicability, assessment authorship, and current evidence validity. Artifact maturity, producer assertion, and central acceptance remain visibly distinct.

p.TOTAL-OBSERVABILITY-DENOMINATOR: Machine views expose every public state and material diagnostic needed to explain strategy and execution lineage, source and proof applicability, lowering, stages and debt, packet context and omissions, forks and dreams, role routing, native dispatch, liveness, retries, resources, economics, holds, stops, completion blockers, and invalidation. Missing data is labeled rather than reconstructed through an implicit model call, and secrets remain outside projections.

p.READER-PREREQUISITES: Human explanations introduce required concepts before use and connect them to the reader's goal. Overview, step-by-step explanation, and source evidence are separate projections. A shorter explanation does not delete obligations or grounds from canonical data, and editing does not require an Owner stop after each passage.

p.MACHINE-ACTIONS: Future IDE actions use typed commands, stable IDs, captured source handles, and expected revision. Renaming changes display text while preserving identity; opening a source does not guess a path from a title. A control action checks backend authority; a button or editable JSON is not an Owner-activation channel. A read-only viewer can operate without command capability.

p.VIEWER-ACCEPTANCE: Future viewer verification covers projection equivalence between full replay and snapshot plus tail, duplicates, gaps, partial tail, stale revision, unknown type, and an unperformed Owner command. It verifies truthful distinctions among pause, resource wait, running job, and accepted task. These scenarios neither run NEXT nor replace final campaign verification.

p.DATA-METHOD-REFERENCE: ZAP-METHODOLOGY.xml defines mandate, stop-rule, recursive-planning, stage, and acceptance meaning. This document makes those concepts externally representable and replayable. Schema validation checks declared data and transitions but does not replace judgment of architecture, mandate completeness, or actual result. Extreme total observability exposes those internal grounds while preserving that boundary.

p.DATA-RUST-STORAGE-REFERENCE: Transactional authority, indexes, bounded queries, snapshots, cold trust, epochs, and portable import follow spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUST-STORAGE#root. Agent messages and lowering subjects follow spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root and spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root.
